Chile]]|[[Canada national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Shaivonte Aician Gilgeous-Alexander''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ʃ|eɪ}} {{respell|SHAY}};{{cite press release |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |website=NBA.com |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 18, 2024}} born July 12, 1998), also known by his initials '''SGA''', is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He is a four-time [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]], a four-time [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA First Team]] member, and two-time [[NBA Most Valuable Player]] (MVP). Gilgeous-Alexander led the Thunder to their first [[2025 NBA Finals|NBA championship]] since [[Seattle SuperSonics relocation to Oklahoma City|relocating]] from [[Seattle]] to [[Oklahoma City]] and was named [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player|Finals MVP]]. Gilgeous-Alexander played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He was selected 11th overall by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the first round of the [[2018 NBA draft]] before being traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on draft night. Following his rookie season, he was traded to the Thunder in July 2019. In the [[2022–23 NBA season]] Gilgeous-Alexander was named to his first [[NBA All-Star Game]] and was voted to the All-NBA First Team, while finishing fourth in the league in scoring with 31.4 points per game. In the [[2023–24 NBA season]] he finished second in MVP voting and third in the league in scoring with 30.1 points per game. In the [[2024–25 NBA season]], Gilgeous-Alexander won the NBA MVP award after [[List of NBA annual scoring leaders|leading the league in scoring]] with an average of 32.7 points per game. He later won the [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player|NBA Finals MVP]] award as the Thunder won the 2025 NBA Finals, becoming the fourth player in NBA history to win the MVP award, Finals MVP award, and scoring title all in the same season. In the [[2025–26 NBA season]] he won his second league MVP award while finishing second in the league in scoring averaging 31.1 points per game.{{Cite web | url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/48795765/sources-thunder-shai-gilgeous-alexander-repeats-nba-mvp | title=Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander repeats as NBA MVP | website=www.espn.com.au}}{{Cite web | url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/45566292/thunder-shai-gilgeous-alexander-named-nba-finals-mvp | title=Thunder's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander named NBA Finals MVP | website=www.espn.com.au}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/shai-gilgeous-alexander-2026-mvp-by-the-numbers|title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander second Kia MVP season by the numbers|website=NBA.com}} With the [[Canada men's national basketball team]], Gilgeous-Alexander won the bronze medal at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] and was named to the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]]. In 2023 and 2025 he received the [[Northern Star Award]] as Canada's Athlete of the Year. ==Early life== Gilgeous-Alexander was born on July 12, 1998, in [[Toronto]], Ontario, and grew up in nearby [[Hamilton, Ontario|Hamilton]].{{Cite web |last=Ewing |first=Lori |date=June 21, 2018 |title=Canadian Shai Gilgeous-Alexander goes 11th in NBA draft, flipped to Clippers |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/canadian-gilgeous-alexander-nba-draft-1.4717462 |access-date=May 4, 2021 |publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation |agency=The Canadian Press}} His mother, [[Charmaine Gilgeous]], is a former professional [[Track and field|track]] athlete who competed in the [[Athletics at the 1992 Summer Olympics – Women's 400 metres|women's 400 metres]] for [[Antigua and Barbuda at the 1992 Summer Olympics|Antigua and Barbuda]] at the [[1992 Summer Olympics]].{{Cite web |last=Loung |first=Steven |date=March 20, 2019 |title=The NBA rookie with the old-school game |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/shai-gilgeous-alexander-clippers-big-read/ |access-date=October 17, 2025 |website=Sportsnet.ca}} His father, Vaughn Alexander, also of Antiguan descent, played high school basketball and won a Toronto city championship while attending [[Georges Vanier Secondary School]] in the early 1990s.{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Jon |date=February 17, 2024 |title=Man of Steeltown |url=https://www.pressreader.com/canada/toronto-star/20240217/282892325577249 |access-date=July 24, 2024 |work=[[The Hamilton Spectator]]}} Gilgeous-Alexander's father coached him during his youth.{{Cite web |last=Tipton |first=Jerry |date=December 13, 2017 |title=Competitive cousins shared a room in high school. UK-Virginia Tech game pits them against each other. |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article189644684.html |access-date=March 3, 2025 |work=Lexington Herald Leader}} He began high school in Hamilton at [[St. Thomas More Catholic Secondary School]] before transferring to nearby [[Sir Allan MacNab Secondary School]]. He later moved to the [[United States]] and attended Hamilton Heights Christian Academy in [[Chattanooga, Tennessee|Chattanooga]], Tennessee, for his [[junior (education year)|junior]] and [[senior (education)|senior]] years to improve his basketball skills, graduating in 2017.{{cite web | last=Wiedmer | first=Mark | title=Wiedmer: Hamilton Heights coach hopes to see former player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander become NBA lottery pick | work=Chattanooga Times Free Press | date=June 21, 2018 | url=https://www.timesfreepress.com/news/2018/jun/21/wiedmer-hamiltheights-coach-hopes-see-former/ | access-date=March 3, 2025}}{{cite web | last=Wiedmer | first=Mark | title=Former Hamilton Heights player now a star at Kentucky | website=Chattanooga Times Free Press | date=March 11, 2018 | url=https://www.timesfreepress.com/news/2018/mar/11/former-hamiltheights-player-now-star-kentucky/ | access-date=March 3, 2025}} ==High school career== Gilgeous-Alexander initially attended [[St. Thomas More Catholic Secondary School]] in [[Hamilton, Ontario|Hamilton]], Ontario. In ninth grade, he did not make the school's junior team and subsequently played on the midget squad,{{Cite news |url=https://www.thespec.com/sports-story/8684906-hamilton-s-shai-gilgeous-alexander-about-to-star-on-nba-stage/ |title=Hamilton's Shai Gilgeous-Alexander about to star on NBA stage |last=Radley |first=Scott |date=June 20, 2018 |work=TheSpec.com |access-date=June 21, 2018 |language=en-CA |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225072034/https://www.thespec.com/sports/basketball/2018/06/21/hamilton-s-shai-gilgeous-alexander-about-to-star-on-nba-stage.html |archive-date=February 25, 2021}} where he was named team MVP and led St. Thomas More to the midget boys' city championship. Gilgeous-Alexander then transferred to nearby [[Sir Allan MacNab Secondary School]] before relocating to the [[United States]] in 2015 to attend Hamilton Heights Christian Academy in [[Chattanooga, Tennessee|Chattanooga]], Tennessee.{{Cite news |last=Wood |first=Russ |date=November 27, 2015 |title=Alexander to Florida |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/alexander-to-florida |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621143339/https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/alexander-to-florida |access-date=July 10, 2017 |archive-date=June 21, 2018 |work=BasketballRecruiting.Rivals.com |url-status=dead}} "I just thought I needed to play better competition," he said. In his senior season, Gilgeous-Alexander averaged 18.4 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game.{{cite news |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article177166321.html |title=After many forks in the road, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander found a basketball home at UK |first=Jerry |last=Tipton |date=October 5, 2017 |newspaper=Lexington Herald-Leader |page=1B}} In early 2016, he participated in the [[Basketball Without Borders]] development camp.{{Cite web |url=http://northpolehoops.com/2016/11/01/kentucky-offers-shai-alexander-after-reopening-recruitment/ |title=Kentucky Offers Shai Alexander After Reopening Recruitment |date=November 1, 2016 |website=Northpolehoops.com |access-date=July 10, 2017}} A four-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] according to [[ESPN]], Gilgeous-Alexander verbally committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]] in November 2015 before decommitting in October 2016.{{Cite web |last=Borzello|first=Jeff|date=November 14, 2016|title=ESPN No. 44 Shai Alexander commits to Kentucky|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/18045597/former-florida-gators-commit-shai-alexander-chooses-kentucky-wildcats|access-date=March 3, 2025|website=[[ESPN]]}} His final five schools were [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], and [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]]. The following month, Gilgeous-Alexander announced his decision to play for the [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky Wildcats]] after signing his [[National Letter of Intent|national letter of intent]] on November 14, 2016. He participated in the 2017 [[Kentucky Derby Festival Basketball Classic]] and was named the [[most valuable player|Most Valuable Player]] (MVP).{{cite web |first=Ben |last=Roberts |title=Kentucky basketball event that has featured NBA stars as recruits canceled for 2018 |date=February 1, 2018 |work=Lexington Herald-Leader |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article197874804.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=May 2, 2023 |quote=UK freshman Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was the most valuable player of last year’s event.}} At the 2017 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], Gilgeous-Alexander represented the World Select Team and scored 11 points in 21 minutes of play.{{Cite news |url=https://www.usab.com/mens/nike-hoop-summit/stats.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726041200/http://www.usab.com/mens/nike-hoop-summit/stats.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 26, 2014 |title=Nike Hoop Summit |access-date=July 11, 2017 |language=en-US}} ==College career== Gilgeous-Alexander started the [[2017–18 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2017–18 season]] with the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] as a [[Substitution (sport)|reserve]], sitting behind freshman [[point guard]] [[Quade Green]], but still averaged over 30 minutes per game. After a loss to [[2017–18 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]], Alexander recorded 24 points, five rebounds, and four assists against [[2017–18 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]] on December 29, 2017.{{cite web |title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4278073/shai-gilgeous-alexander |publisher=ESPN |access-date=February 15, 2018}} When he first stepped on the [[University of Kentucky]]'s campus, Gilgeous-Alexander had long hair. However, he cut his hair early in the season and some say this started his progression from [[sixth man]] to [[Starting lineup|starting]] [[point guard]].{{cite web |last1=Tucker |first1=Kyle |title=Kentucky basketball: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander cuts his hair, then carves up Louisville |url=https://www.seccountry.com/kentucky/kentucky-basketball-shai-gilgeous-alexander-burns-louisville |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180227034457/https://www.seccountry.com/kentucky/kentucky-basketball-shai-gilgeous-alexander-burns-louisville |archive-date=February 27, 2018 |access-date=February 15, 2018 |website=SEC Country}} He continued to lead the team for the following two games, scoring 21 points against [[2017–18 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]] and 18 against [[2017–18 LSU Tigers basketball team|LSU]]. He was a consistent contributor to a "struggling" Kentucky team that had a four-game losing streak during the season. He became a starter along with four other freshmen: [[Hamidou Diallo]], [[Nick Richards]], [[Kevin Knox II]], and [[P. J. Washington]]. Despite their losses, his PPG shot up to 12.9 along with 3.8 rebounds and 4.6 assists. Gilgeous-Alexander had a great [[2018 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], earning [[Most valuable player|Most Valuable Player]] (MVP) honours, and continued that momentum into the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. After playing great basketball in the first two rounds against [[2017–18 Davidson Wildcats men's basketball team|Davidson]] and [[2017–18 Buffalo Bulls men's basketball team|Buffalo]], Kentucky lost to [[2017–18 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]] in the Sweet 16. Gilgeous-Alexander's final [[college basketball]] moment was a missed three-point attempt at the buzzer. He concluded his freshman season and, consequently, his college career, having played 37 games with 24 starts, averaging 14.4 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 5.1 assists per game while shooting 48.5 percent from the field.{{Cite web |title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 2017-18 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/shai-gilgeous-alexander-1/gamelog/2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205104201/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/shai-gilgeous-alexander-1/gamelog/2018 |archive-date=December 5, 2025 |access-date=December 5, 2025 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}} After the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]], Gilgeous-Alexander declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] on April 9, 2018.{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Kentucky freshman guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander to enter draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23094736/shai-gilgeous-alexander-kentucky-wildcats-entering-nba-draft |access-date=April 10, 2018 |publisher=ESPN |date=April 9, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Clippers (2018–2019)=== [[File:Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 2 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Gilgeous-Alexander with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in 2018]] Gilgeous-Alexander was selected 11th overall by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the first round of the [[2018 NBA draft]] on June 21, 2018. On draft night, he was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for the 12th overall pick, [[Miles Bridges]], and two future second-round picks.{{Cite web |last=Reed |first=Steve |date=June 21, 2018 |title=LA Clippers swap picks with Charlotte Hornets to acquire Shai Gilgeous-Alexander |url=https://www.nba.com/news/report-la-clippers-swap-picks-charlotte-hornets-get-shai-gilgeous-alexander |archive-date= |access-date=December 6, 2025 |website=[[NBA]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Gilgeous-Alexander participated in the [[2018 NBA Summer League]] with the Los Angeles Clippers in the [[2018 NBA Summer League#Las Vegas NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]]. In Game 4 of the series on April 21, he recorded a then-career-high 25 points in a 113–105 loss to the Warriors.{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201904210LAC.html|title=2019 NBA Western Conference First Round Game 4: Golden State Warriors at Los Angeles Clippers Box Score, April 21, 2019|date=April 21, 2019|access-date=November 27, 2025|website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2019–present)=== ====2019–20: Improving as a sophomore==== The [[Los Angeles Clippers]] traded Gilgeous-Alexander along with [[Danilo Gallinari]], five first-round draft picks, and the rights to swap two other first-round picks to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] [[Paul George]] on July 10, 2019.{{cite press release |title=L.A. Clippers Acquire Six-Time NBA All-Star Paul George |date=July 10, 2019 |publisher=Los Angeles Clippers |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-acquire-six-time-nba-all-star-paul-george |access-date=July 10, 2019}} On October 8, Gilgeous-Alexander made his [[2019–20 Oklahoma City Thunder season#Preseason|preseason]] debut with the Thunder against the [[2019–20 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]], recording 24 points and four rebounds in a 119–104 win. On December 22, Gilgeous-Alexander scored a then-career-high 32 points with five assists, three rebounds, and two steals in a 118–112 win over the [[2019–20 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].{{Cite web |date=December 22, 2019 |title=Gilgeous-Alexander helps Thunder beat Clippers 118–112 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161084 |access-date=December 23, 2019 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} On January 13, 2020, Gilgeous-Alexander recorded his first career [[Double-double#Triple-double|triple-double]] with 20 points, 10 assists, and a career-high 20 rebounds in a 117–104 win over the [[2019–20 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]]. His 6-foot 11 inch (2.11 m) wingspan, body control, speed, and embrace of defensive contact make him one of the best [[Slasher (basketball)|slashers]] in the history of the NBA, boasting a 68 percent career field goal percentage within three feet of the basket.{{Cite web|title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gilgesh01.html|website=basketball-reference.com|access-date=June 23, 2025}} Gilgeous-Alexander is regarded as a two-way player: he earned All-Defensive Team votes from 2023 to 2026 and placed 7th in the voting for the 2024 [[Defensive Player of the Year Award]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/awards/awards_2024.html |title=2023-24 NBA Awards Voting |website=basketball-reference |access-date=June 23, 2025}} Gilgeous-Alexander has earned widespread praise across the NBA for his leadership, work ethic, and maturity. Former teammates [[Patrick Beverley]] and [[Chris Paul]] recognized his relentless work ethic and dedication to the game from beginning of his career, with Beverley comparing Gilgeous-Alexander's mindset to the likes of [[Kobe Bryant]] and [[Michael Jordan]].{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Prateek |date=June 16, 2025 |title=Patrick Beverley Shocked Rookie Shai Gilgeous-Alexander By Comparing Him To Michael Jordan And Kobe Bryant |url=https://thesportsrush.com/nba-news-patrick-beverley-shocked-rookie-shai-gilgeous-alexander-by-comparing-him-to-michael-jordan-and-kobe-bryant/ |access-date=July 21, 2025 |website=The SportsRush |language=en}}{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZZrMxLbdj4M |title=Chris Paul applauds Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's selflessness & work ethic {{!}} NBA Countdown |date=May 22, 2025 |last=NBA on ESPN |access-date=July 21, 2025 |via=YouTube}} Thunder head coach [[Mark Daigneault]] has praised Gilgeous-Alexander for his composure and selflessness, highlighting how he leads by example on and off the court.{{Cite web |last=Yasis |first=Nathan |date=March 24, 2025 |title=Mark Daigneault gets 100% real about Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's leadership |url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/oklahoma-city-thunder/thunder-news-mark-daigneault-real-shai-gilgeous-alexander-leadership |access-date=July 21, 2025 |website=ClutchPoints {{!}} Oklahoma City Thunder News |language=en}} Gilgeous-Alexander has faced heavy fan criticism on [[social media]] for his high free throw numbers and tendency to embellish contact when driving. He led the NBA in total free throws made from the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022–23 season]] to the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], though he has never led in free throws attempted. Former NBA player [[Richard Jefferson]] addressed the narrative of Gilgeous-Alexander being a "free-throw merchant" to discredit his offensive prowess, saying, "Shai is one of the most impressive people that I've ever talked to. I asked him about the free throws, and he's like, 'Yeah. You know what's crazy about it is that two years ago, I averaged almost 11 free throws a game but we finished 10th and no one cared. When I wasn't sending their best favorite player home when I wasn't sending their team home, then no one cared that I was shooting 11 free throws a night and scoring this amount of points.' Within days of moving in, Gilgeous-Alexander and his partner vacated the residence due to ongoing security concerns related to Pleterski's highly publicized fraud and bankruptcy case, which had led to threats and repeated visits from investors seeking Pleterski. Gilgeous-Alexander subsequently filed a lawsuit to rescind the purchase, alleging that the seller, who had [[Lease#Leasing property|leased]] the property to Pleterski, failed to disclose the property's connection to the trader and the associated safety risks.{{cite web |last=Brockbank |first=Nicole |date=November 2, 2023 |title=The basketball star, the Crypto King and the $8.4M mansion |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/nba-star-lawsuit-void-purchase-mansion-ontario-crypto-king-1.7015253 |access-date=November 18, 2023 |work=[[CBC News]]}}{{cite web |last=Austen |first=Ian |date=November 15, 2023 |title=For an N.B.A. Star, a Dream House Became a Nightmare |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/11/15/world/canada/shai-gilgeous-alexander-house-crypto.html |access-date=November 18, 2023 |work=[[The New York Times]]}} The court ruled in favour of Gilgeous-Alexander, finding fraudulent misrepresentation on the part of the seller and awarded him damages for mortgage and insurance payments incurred. Consequently, the purchase was reversed, and the seller's appeal was denied. The case set a precedent in [[Canadian property law|Ontario real estate law]] by expanding the scope of required property disclosures to include latent safety risks beyond the physical condition of the property.{{Cite web |last=Brockbank |first=Nicole |date=December 7, 2023 |title=Canadian NBA star wins lawsuit to undo purchase of mansion where Ontario Crypto King lived |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/basketball-star-shai-gilgeous-alexander-wins-lawsuit-undo-home-sale-1.7052140 |access-date=February 22, 2025 |website=[[CBC News]]}}{{cite web |last1=Arnold |first1=Chris |date=August 13, 2024 |title=Ontario court dismisses appeal on Burlington home previously owned by crypto king, NBA player |url=https://www.burlingtontoday.com/local-news/ontario-court-dismisses-appeal-on-burlington-home-previously-owned-by-crypto-king-nba-player-9345400 |access-date=February 22, 2025 |website=BurlingtonToday.com |language=}} Gilgeous-Alexander's home in [[Nichols Hills, Oklahoma|Nichols Hills]], Oklahoma, was [[Burglary|burglarized]] while he was at the [[Paycom Center]] in downtown [[Oklahoma City]], playing the [[2025–26 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]] on October 30, 2025.{{Cite web |last=Nagel |first=Cody |date=October 31, 2025 |title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's home burglarized during Thunder game against Wizards |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/shai-gilgeous-alexanders-home-burglarized-during-thunder-game-against-wizards/ |access-date=November 24, 2025 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}} == Personal life == Gilgeous-Alexander is of [[Antiguans and Barbudans|Antiguan]] descent.
